questions.question: When is a set $A$ called finite?
options: When it has $n$ distinct elements for some $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
When every element is a real number at most some $n\in\mathbb{N}$.
When each of its elements is a natural number.
When its elements can be listed as $a_1,a_2,a_3,\ldots$.

questions.question: What notation is used for the number of elements of a finite set $A$?
Which set is finite?
Which set is identified as infinite?
What is meant by saying that a finite set has well-defined cardinality?
options: Its largest element is its size $|A|$.
Its size can be written as $|A| = n$.
Its size depends on the order of listing.

questions.question: Suppose $A\subseteq\mathbb{R}$ contains an element greater than every proposed real upper bound. Which statement is guaranteed?
options: The elements of A can be listed in a finite list.
A is finite but has no largest element.

questions.question: If $A = \{a,b,c,d\}$ with four distinct elements, what is $|A|$?
Which conclusion follows if a set cannot be placed in bijection with any finite set?
Why is the word ‘distinct’ important for finite set?
options: It forbids writing a set such as $\{1,1,2\}$ at all.
Repeated descriptions should not inflate the count.
It means each listed copy, as in $\{1,1,2\}$, counts separately.
It means the order of listing elements matters.

questions.question: Which statement is the safest reading of ‘otherwise, $A$ is infinite’?
options: If no natural $n$ counts its distinct elements, $A$ is infinite.
If $A$ has more than $n$ elements for one $n$, $A$ is infinite.
If $A$ contains a non-natural number such as $\pi$, then $A$ is infinite.
If no finite list of $A$ is known yet, $A$ is infinite.

questions.question: A student claims that $\mathbb{N}$ is finite because its first three elements are $0,1,2$. What is the issue?
options: Listing a few elements does not exhaust $\mathbb{N}$.
$\mathbb{N}$ is finite, but it has more than three elements.
$\mathbb{N}$ is finite, since each of its elements is finite.
$\mathbb{N}$ has no smallest element, so no list can start.

questions.question: Which set has cardinality $3$?
Let $A=\{2,4,\ldots,2n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. How many distinct elements does $A$ contain?
Does every non-empty finite set of real numbers have a maximum?
options: Only if all elements are positive
Only if it is an interval

questions.question: What does the distinction between finite and infinite sets concern?
options: Sets with finitely many elements versus the rest
Bounded subsets of $\mathbb{R}$ versus unbounded ones
Sets containing zero versus sets not containing zero
Sets with a largest element versus those without

questions.question: Is every subset of a finite set finite?
For finite sets $A$ and $B$, which expression is always an upper bound for $|A\cup B|$?
Is the set of natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ finite or infinite?
In terms of counting, what does it mean for a set $A$ to be infinite?
options: It has more elements than any set of real numbers.
It can be paired one-to-one with $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for a large $n$.
Each of its proper subsets must be a finite set.
It cannot be paired one-to-one with $\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for any $n$.
